(Sorry for the lengthy post, but wanted to share my thought process as well as to share the solution!)

As a person who tries to be well prepared without being obsessive about it, I still try to take some time to think about the things I might want or need that might not be readily available during an "event."

While doing the laundry, I happened to look at the bottle of Clorox on the shelf and thought, "Gee...that bottle's getting pretty old. Sure, I could go down to the grocery store and pick up a bottle...but what if I couldn't? What if I needed some to purify my water in an emergency? Would this stuff even work? Is it possible to make my own easily and cheaply without having to use/store dangerous chemicals?"

**The answer to that last question is, absolutely, YES.** Turns out all you need is a pencil, water, titanium wire, a 9V battery (or other voltage source) and some wires with clips to connect things. Maybe a little table salt too...but probably not.

Here's a YouTube video outlining the process: [Portable Salt Chlorine Generator.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P-Ihaq2f3EI)

[Edit] Wow. Just. Wow. The intent of my post was not to ignite a shit storm. It wasn't to infer that you can be out in the woods, in need of chlorine, pull a pencil and some wire out of your ass and save civilization. And it certainly wasn't to discount any other methods of purifying water, especially boiling.

It was to mention an inexpensive and easy way to produce chlorine if and when you need it and it wasn't readily available. Nothing more.
An easy, cheap, on-demand way to make your own chlorine for water purification.

Better answer is to buy one and keep it in your bug out bag.
